newsitem.title: USA: Calif. transit agency settles charges-U.S.Attorney.
newsitem.headline: Calif. transit agency settles charges-U.S.Attorney.

text.p: The Santa Cruz, Calif., Metropolitan Transit District will pay $2.7 million to settle allegations that it submitted false claims for federal disaster relief funding, federal prosecutors said on Tuesday.

The payment settles allegations that the transit district submitted false claims to the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) for federal disaster relief funds in the wake of the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake, said Michael Yamaguchi, U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of California.
The Santa Cruz transit district submitted claims to FEMA to recover over $4.1 million for damages allegedly caused by the October 1989 earthquake, Yamaguchi said.
Among the claims that the transit district submitted to FEMA were claims for cracks in underground storage tanks that the transit district had used to store diesel and waste oil.
But an investigation conducted by FEMA revealed that there had been major leaks to the underground storage tanks prior to the earthquake, Yamaguchi said.
The $2,669,074 settlement includes about $1.8 million to repay FEMA for funding storage tank repairs and about $900,000 in penalties for making the false claims.
"The transit district has been forthright in acknowledging its liability and taking actions to correct the problems caused by the inflated claims," Yamaguchi said.
